preamble: Each clue contains an extra word; these words’ middle letters give a hint to the theme. Two unclued entries are thematic. After filling the grid, solvers must change ten letters to make six new entries, providing a symmetrical representation of the theme.

messages.text: CHORUS OF STEALERS XXVI ACROSS VIII

clue.text: Argument with country club having special backing for Go West concert

definitions.note: to go west is an idiom for to die, a verb phrase like the answer

indicators.note: backing means the whole string built so far is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
the United Nations is in effect a club whose members are countries

explanation.surface: A row at a country club over a special Village People-style concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concert' is the extra word; its middle letter C joins the hidden message. 'Go West' is the Village People song, but here it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are slang for dying, so going west and this idiom are interchangeable.

clue.text: Holy man's depressive illness paradoxically starts to help unbelievers

parts.note: SAD is seasonal affective disorder, winter depression

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each of the following words

parts.note: the words whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A holy man whose gloom paradoxically leads him to help non-believers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paradoxically' is the extra word; its middle letter X joins the message.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man who has renounced worldly life.

clue.text: Rowdy boxer drinking reporter's tea wrongfully

indicators.note: drinking means the rowdy word swallows the next piece

parts.note: unruly means disorderly and rowdy

indicators.note: reporter's signals a sound-alike: the word tea is said aloud as a letter

parts.note: tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A boisterous boxer knocks back a journalist's cup of tea, unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' is the extra word, giving X to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Untruly means falsely or not in accordance with the facts, so wrongly.

clue.text: Knowing lover, move swiftly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for sharp, streetwise and knowing
second meaning: to go very fast

explanation.surface: A savvy lover makes a quick getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lover' is the extra word, giving V to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means shrewd and hard to fool in British slang, and the verb means to rush along.

clue.text: Projections of other light reflecting for one second

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small electric light

indicators.note: reflecting means the abbreviation is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: e.g. (exempli gratia) means for example, i.e. for one

explanation.surface: Something about how projected images of a second light bounce back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' is the extra word, giving H to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Ledges are shelves or ridges jutting out from a wall or cliff, i.e. projections.

clue.text: Allowed to be on upcoming Legislative Assembly committee

parts.note: the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the letters run upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: LA is a standard abbreviation for Legislative Assembly

explanation.surface: Permission to sit on a forthcoming parliamentary committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committee' is the extra word, giving I to the message. In cricket the on side is the leg side, the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal means permitted by law, so allowed.

clue.text: Less steady ride, struggling over extreme roads

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
struggling means in difficulty, so the letters of ride are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
OTT, over the top, means extreme or excessive

explanation.surface: A shakier journey, battling over the worst of the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roads' is the extra word, giving A to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty can mean unsteady on one's feet, an older sense beside its usual meaning of eccentric.

clue.text: Another world record, including 10-0 over City before final matches

indicators.note: over in a down clue means sitting above, so this comes first
before means the city comes ahead of the final piece
including means the record's letters hold the score inside them

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
ten is X in Roman numerals and nil looks like the letter O
LA is Los Angeles
net means final, as in a net result after deductions

explanation.surface: A sports report: a world-record 10-0 win over City before the final matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' is the extra word, giving C to the message; 'world record' looks like one unit but 'world' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun, another world.

clue.text: Poem's dead funny, apart from prose introduction

indicators.note: apart from means leaving something out, here a single letter of the funny word
the introduction of a word is its opening letter, the one dropped

parts.note: witty means amusing, clever and funny

explanation.surface: A literary judgement that a poem is hilarious, unlike its prose preface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prose' is the extra word, giving O to the message; 'dead funny' looks like one phrase but splits into D and a word for amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditty is a short simple poem or song.

clue.text: Worry further, mostly about storage unit

parts.note: angst is anxiety or worry

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the shortened word is read backwards
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: more means further or additional

explanation.surface: Fretting even more about a storage unit, perhaps a full lock-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storage' is the extra word, giving R to the message; 'storage unit' looks like the definition but only 'unit' is.
explanation.definitionFit: The angstrom is a tiny unit of length, one ten-billionth of a metre, used for atomic distances.

clue.text: Uproar and disapproval expressed about rum smuggler mainly

indicators.note: about means the sound of disapproval goes round the other piece

parts.note: tut is the clicking noise made to express disapproval

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a mule is someone who carries drugs or contraband across a border

explanation.surface: A noisy scandal over a man running illicit rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the extra word; its middle letter U joins the message.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumult is a loud confused commotion, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: Coming up against informer's warrant card

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters climb upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: to can mean against or touching, as in standing back to back
a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: A detective's warrant card turns up against an informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warrant' is the extra word, giving R to the message; 'warrant card' looks like a police ID but only 'card' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot card belongs to the deck used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Portugal supporter covering unusual top weakly

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

indicators.note: covering means the supporter's letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: an ally is someone who backs you
a lid is the top of a box or jar

explanation.surface: A Portugal fan wearing an odd top cheers half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' is the extra word, giving S to the message; it looks like an anagram signal for 'top' but plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid means pale and lacking vigour, so doing something pallidly is doing it feebly.

clue.text: Sheila's nervous, still not over accepting love

definitions.note: Sheila is Australian slang for a woman, flagging an Australian word

indicators.note: accepting means the reversed word takes the next letter inside itself
over tells us to turn the word for still upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not done yet'
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: An Australian woman remains jittery, not yet over a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' is the extra word, giving O to the message. 'Sheila's' signals an Australian word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang this word means restless, edgy or anxious.

clue.text: Mostly getting better for everyone available for impromptu dinner?

definitions.note: the definition is really 'available for dinner', with 'impromptu' the extra word inside it

indicators.note: mostly means most of the phrase, dropping its last letter

parts.note: on the mend means recovering from illness
U is the film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Nearly recovered and free for anyone who fancies a spur-of-the-moment meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impromptu' is the extra word, giving O to the message, so the definition reads 'available for dinner?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes on the menu are ones a restaurant offers, so available to order for a meal.

clue.text: Ruby, the woman with magnificent jewellery, is a distraction

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour
her is the pronoun for a woman already mentioned
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Ruby, dripping in magnificent jewels, draws every eye away from what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'magnificent' is the extra word; its middle letter F joins the message. 'Ruby' looks like a woman's name but gives a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is something that misleads or distracts attention, originally a smoked fish dragged to throw hounds off a scent.

clue.text: On USA vacation earlier eating fish and duck

indicators.note: eating means the emptied word takes the fish inside it
on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters
vacation is the emptying of a place, so only the shell of the word stays

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are kept
the ide is a freshwater fish, a favourite in crosswords

explanation.surface: An American holiday where earlier we ate fish and duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'USA' is the extra word, giving S to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Cachet of setter bothered housing councillor and journalist

indicators.note: bothered means flustered or disturbed, so the letters of setter are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A flustered crossword setter puts up a councillor and a reporter, gaining prestige.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' is the extra word, giving S to the message; it looks like a container signal but does nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility or prestige among fashionable or young people, the kind of status cachet implies.

clue.text: English bosun heading off to provide assistance for swimmer

indicators.note: heading off means the phrase loses its first letter

parts.note: to help out is to give assistance

explanation.surface: An English boatswain sets off to help someone struggling in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bosun' is the extra word, giving S to the message; 'swimmer' is a fish, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The eelpout is an eel-like fish of cold seas, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Cancelled vital services for fear that society shifts rightwards

indicators.note: shifts rightwards means the society letter leaves its place and moves along to the end

parts.note: lest means for fear that
the society letter again, now in its new place at the end

explanation.surface: Essential services axed for fear that society will drift to the right politically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' is the extra word, giving T to the message; the definition is 'Cancelled services'. The final S is the society letter in its new place. In tennis a let is a serve that is void and taken again.
explanation.definitionFit: A let in tennis is a serve that clips the net and is annulled, so lets are voided serves.

clue.text: Uncovered condition of horses, limping around softly on right side primarily

indicators.note: around means the limping word goes round the soft letter

parts.note: lame means limping
p is piano, the musical direction for softly

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter of side

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A vet uncovers a horse's ailment: it limps, favouring its right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' is the extra word, giving V to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampers, or lampas, is a swelling of the roof of a horse's mouth behind the front teeth.

clue.text: Pearl somehow limiting delay in adrenal disease

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the jumbled letters form a boundary round the other piece
somehow says the letters of Pearl are rearranged in some way

parts.note: taken as written
a lag is a delay, as in time lag

explanation.surface: Something about Pearl and a delay in an adrenal illness diagnosis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrenal' is the extra word, giving E to the message; 'adrenal disease' tempts the solver to look for an adrenal condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellagra is a disease caused by lack of niacin, marked by dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

clue.text: Information on adviser in charge of what's inherited

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching an adjective answer

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Briefing notes from a financial adviser handling an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adviser' is the extra word, giving I to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Genic means relating to genes, the units by which traits are inherited.

clue.text: Rap artist taking in European capital in comeback — sucker!

indicators.note: taking in means the artist's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock artist

indicators.note: in comeback means the capital is read backwards, coming back on itself

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A rapper's European comeback tour, with a jeer at someone gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' is the extra word, giving A to the message; 'sucker' looks like an insult but means a fish that clings on.
explanation.definitionFit: The remora, or suckerfish, attaches itself to sharks and other large fish with a sucking disc on its head.

clue.text: Genuinely lacking energy to recover faith

indicators.note: lacking means the word goes without the energy letter

parts.note: really means genuinely or truly

explanation.surface: Truly drained of energy, someone struggles to regain their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faith' is the extra word, giving I to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover strength or spirits after a setback, as a patient or a market rallies.

clue.text: Condemn study after bringing in Welsh university

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom

indicators.note: bringing in means the word takes the university letter inside it

parts.note: once can mean after, as in 'once you've finished, go home'

explanation.surface: Condemning a course of study once a Welsh university is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' is the extra word, giving L to the message; 'after' looks like a placing signal but supplies a word of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly.

clue.text: Attempt to turn in wife — despicable person

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible, untrustworthy man

explanation.surface: A cad tries to shop his own wife to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attempt' is the extra word, giving E to the message, and it makes 'to turn' look like part of a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn or pivot, as a line of soldiers wheels round a fixed point.

clue.text: Moderately conservative people in general remaining tense

parts.note: we can mean people as a whole, as in 'we all need sleep'

explanation.surface: A political profile: moderate Tories as a group stay on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remaining' is the extra word, giving I to the message. A wet, in British politics, is a moderate member of the Conservative party, a term from the Thatcher years.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher's allies called her party's moderates wets, so wet describes a mildly Conservative stance.

clue.text: Wood cuts weirdly if warped

indicators.note: warped means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter's grumble that timber cuts badly once it has warped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weirdly' is the extra word, giving R to the message; it looks like the anagram signal, but 'warped' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Fustic is the yellow wood of a tropical American tree, once used for dye.

clue.text: Meet outside of factory after current issue stops tests

indicators.note: after means the outer letters come later in the answer
stops means plugs a gap, so the current letter sits inside the tests

parts.note: SATs are standardised school tests
I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: Workers gather outside a factory after a current issue halts testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is the extra word, giving S to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a need or demand is to meet it, as in meeting a target.
